description: cert_name_constraints (line 627) calls .ok() on NameConstraints::from_der — a DER decode error silently returns None, causing the NC extension to be skipped entirely. If a CA cert has a malformed but critical NameConstraints extension, check_critical_extensions will catch it (since NC is in HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS). But if the extension is non-critical AND malformed AND the caller's x509 library returns a non-critical extension, the NC constraints are silently ignored. Additionally, if the NameConstraints DER is syntactically valid but semantically wrong (e.g., GeneralSubtree with non-zero minimum/maximum), the silencing loses the error. For a security-critical extension, silent-discard is a footgun. Future maintainers copy the .ok() pattern to other security extensions. Mitigation: propagate the error or at minimum log in debug builds.
title: decoding errors in cert_name_constraints silently treated as absent
